pending_diagnosis: DIAGNOSIS: Anti-NMDA Receptor Encephalitis (secondary to an underlying mature ovarian teratoma) THE SMOKING GUN: The progression from acute psychiatric symptoms to orofacial dyskinesias, autonomic instability, and the pathognomonic 'extreme delta brush' on EEG, confirmed by pelvic ultrasound demonstrating a mature cystic teratoma. PATHOPHYSIOLOGY: Autoantibodies (IgG) target the GluN1 subunit of N-methyl-D-aspartate (NMDA) receptors in the central nervous system, frequently triggered by ectopic neural tissue expressing NMDA receptors within an occult ovarian teratoma. This cross-reactivity causes cross-linking, internalization, and severe depletion of NMDA receptors on GABAergic interneurons, resulting in disinhibition of frontostriatal circuits, severe autonomic collapse, and catastrophic neuropsychiatric dysfunction.
